sp.deepHead: [STORY RECORD · BACKGROUND] What has been settled so far. Unless told otherwise, stay consistent with it. Do not copy or explain it. Characters know only what they know.
sp.midHead: [STATE AT THE END OF THE LAST REPLY · REFERENCE] The starting point for this reply. If the user asks to change the time, place or scene, follow that; otherwise continue from here. Props, numbers and dates already written: use only when needed, do not repeat them.
sp.nowHead: [THIS REPLY · LINES AND LEAK LEVEL] What changed after the last reply and the lines to keep in this one. The user's instruction comes first. How to write the scene is free. Do not turn this note into dialogue or explain it.

sp.notHere: {name}: no {what} in this story so far
sp.timeSkip: Time skip: {s} since the last reply. Open this reply after that gap and let the passing of time show

loreGuide: What the sheet is — the story's ground (people, ties, secrets), one "key: value" per line. Only the classifier reads it; it is not passed to the main model as is. Meatball builds each reply's "lines and leak level" from the ties written here (tie · texture · inner · sore · hide).

Where it is saved — "Save to this chat" keeps it for this chat only; "Save as character default" for every chat with this character. This chat's wins. With neither, a lorebook entry titled "meatball lore" in the character's book is read (keep that entry switched off: Meatball still reads it and the main model does not).

Draft — one AI call, only when pressed (the classifier's connection profile). It reads the card's description, personality and scenario plus the character's lorebook entries (except ones mentioning Meatball), up to 24,000 characters, and is told to write only what the source states. The result is appended below and saved nowhere until you press a save button. The draft is always in English (both Korean and English keys are read). A Korean sheet is fine: the classifier reads it as is, and it is turned into English only where it goes into the main model's note (names kept).
Lines that matter most — tie · texture · inner · sore · hide · deep. With them, lines and leak level go in before any record builds up.

New in v0.7 — hide: A>B = what (what A keeps from B; every reply while both are here: "may come close, is not seen") · unknown: Name = what (not decided by anyone yet, you included; every reply: "behavior only, nobody guesses or explains"; the classifier does not guess a cause either) · channel: Name = voice, hands (where that person's feeling leaks; added when an inner or texture line comes).

v0.8 vault · sparks · lines — vault: Name (or A-B) = what stays hidden | signs: words that give it away (Korean and English) | shows: what may show | opens: when. The hidden part never reaches the main model; only "shows" does. Note lines holding a sign are dropped by code; a new reply holding a sign, or the guard catching "revealed / settled / rushed" with a quote, puts ⚠ in the status line. Put where the story should end up (e.g. they fall in love) in the vault too: hidden = the destination, signs = confess, kiss…, shows = the stage now (e.g. only deniable moments). · self: Name = hums while working, loves sweets (sparks: the old self slips once) · line: Name = coming into the back room (when the person's message touches the line or runs ahead of the tie, a refusal is allowed in that reply).

v0.9 — add | cover: what those around believe to a vault line so the story does not invent its own explanation. avoid: who would notice>vault person = why they stop asking (fear, pride, chose to believe). Add | release: condition to a line: the refusal lifts when that is quoted in the text. A vault with | opens: condition opens the same way. A leaked reply that stays while two more replies follow opens that vault.

v0.9 harsh · fall · old things — harsh: A>B = A's attitude toward B (blunt, mocking, pushing away) | limit: the line never crossed; crossing it raises ⚠. fall: A>B = how A shows it once fallen | opens: condition | keeps: what stays even then. Meatball counts the kinds of things the two went through, days and replies; when the condition is confirmed by a quote, 💗 shows in the bar. Pressing it (or auto in settings) lets the character come undone while keeping what is listed in keeps. Switch on the "old things" group to have small things from long ago resurface when they overlap the scene. Example: harsh: A>B = pushes back at every word | limit: never hits · fall: A>B = cannot look away | opens: sees B hurt | keeps: the same curt voice
If it is wrong — when the scene's text differs, the text wins. Lines that could not be read are listed under the box.

lore.head: [USUAL SETTING] Background outside the story. If the current scene differs, [CURRENT STATE] and [NEW TEXT] win.
lore.headDeep: [USUAL SETTING · DETAIL] Background outside the story, for context only. If the text differs, the text wins.
lore.notPeople: [NOT CHARACTERS] These names are a title, a world or an off-screen director. Never use them in with, wear or any key.

guard.head: [GUARD] Kept by the writer. Do not use these in any other line of your answer. G = entry: who | what is kept | signs that give it away · H = the writer's rule: name | what to avoid
guard.rules:
Before <mb>, write <guard>…</guard>. One line per entry that the NEW replies touched, else "none":
G1: revealed | "quote"   (the text states or plainly shows what is kept)
G1: settled | "quote"    (the text decides an open question the entry keeps open)
G1: rushed | "quote"     (the text jumps to where the entry says the story should only end up)
G1: clue | "quote"       (the text adds a sign pointing to what is kept, where someone who does not know could see it)
G1: near | "quote"       (someone in the text is reasoning their way toward what is kept)
The quote is copied from the text, 4-12 words. Plain hints with no new sign: "none".
guard.rules2:
F1: crossed | "quote"   (the character went past this limit)
K1: lost | "quote"      (the character is shown without this: it is gone from voice or manner)
guard.limitDefault: no hitting or harm, no tearing the other down as a person
guard.rules3: H1: broke | "quote"     (a NEW reply does what this rule asks to avoid; judge the meaning, not the words)
